about: Process plan for the L&L spacer (Abstandhalter, 1007224) in 6061-T6: a blank sawn from round bar on the band saw, turned on the shop's Haas ST-25 in two setups, one per spigot, in its Kitagawa 3-jaw chuck's soft jaws, its five bolt holes drilled on the VF-2 in the Kurt D688, then the bench and inspection. Its real routing isn't known; the part record's machines_likely is saw, lathe, VMC, inspection. Written by Claude from the drawing (314-092-59935-10) and the STEP model; every feature below is checked against the model by moonshot/planning/validate.py. Model frame: Y is the axis. The first spigot, Ø31.500 g6, runs from Y=0 (its end) to Y=3.2, the flange, Ø63.0, from 3.2 to 12.2, the second spigot from 12.2 to 15.4; each spigot has a 0.5 x 45 deg chamfer on its end and an R0.4 at its root, the flange a 0.5 x 45 deg chamfer on each outside edge. The five Ø6.6 holes go through the flange on a 25 mm radius: four at 45 deg (X and Z ±17.68) and one at Z=+25. Op 10 holds the blank by its far end, which Op 20 faces and turns away, so the jaws' marks go with it; Op 20 holds the part by the flange Op 10 finished.

stock.from: sawn from the bar on the band saw [proposed: 2-1/2 in bar, 0.25 mm a side over the Ø63.0, which is ±0.3 (ISO 2768-m); 1 in long: 17.4 mm out of the jaws for the first spigot and the flange, 8 mm in them]

faces_out.-Y: an end 17.4 mm out, the other against the jaws' step
faces_out.+Y: flipped, the finished flange in the jaws against their step

operations.what: Cut the 1 in blank from the bar

setups.title: Op 10: first spigot and the outside

workholding.jaws: soft jaws bored Ø63.5, 8 mm deep, to a step
workholding.note: In the Kitagawa's soft jaws, bored to the bar's Ø63.5 and 8 mm deep to a step the blank's end seats on (model Y 16.9 to 24.9, the blank from -0.5 before its facing): 17.4 mm out from the jaws' front, the first spigot's 3.2 and the flange's 9.0 with 0.5 to face and 4.7 of clearance to the jaws. Boring the soft jaws isn't a step, as G1's soft jaws (ll-1007223 Op 20). The jaws hold the end Op 20 cuts away

wcs.z: the blank's end, less 0.5 mm for the facing
wcs.by: the CCGT roughing tool touched on the blank's end

operations.what: Face the end and rough the first spigot, the flange's face and the outside to 2 mm past the flange, leaving 0.25 mm

speeds.source: 300 m/min, the shop's rule for carbide in aluminium (moonshot/sim/cam.py MATERIALS: Machinery's Handbook, the lower half); 1,500 rpm at the bar's Ø63.5. [proposed: 0.25 mm/rev and 2 mm deep, the middle of a polished CCGT 09T308's roughing range in aluminium]

operations.what: Finish the first spigot to Ø31.500 g6 (-0.009/-0.025) with its 0.5 x 45° chamfer and R0.4 root, the flange's face, and the Ø63.0 with its 0.5 x 45° chamfer

speeds.source: 300 m/min as rough's. [proposed: 0.08 mm/rev, a fifth of the 0.4 nose's radius, for the g6's finish; 0.25 mm deep]. The R0.4 roots are the DCGT's own 0.4 mm nose

workholding.note: Flipped into the same soft jaws: the flange's finished Ø63.0 in their Ø63.5 bore, which they close 0.25 mm further on, its faced side against their step, so they grip 8 mm of its 9 (model Y 3.2 to 11.2) and leave its outer chamfer clear. 13.7 mm out from the jaws' front, measured as Op 10's: the 24.9 mm part Op 10 left, its end at Y 24.9, less the jaws' front at Y 11.2 (21.7 measured from their step at Y 3.2). Gripped so, it runs true within the general 0.2 mm (ISO 2768-K); no runout is toleranced between the spigots [proposed]

wcs.z: the finished end, 12.2 mm out from the jaws' step
wcs.by: the CCGT roughing tool touched on the jaws' step face before loading, and moved out by the part's 12.2 mm

operations.what: Face to the 15.4 mm length and rough the second spigot and the flange's other face, leaving 0.25 mm

speeds.source: As Op 10's rough. The end comes down 9.5 mm, faced in 2 mm passes

operations.what: Finish the second spigot to Ø31.500 g6 (-0.009/-0.025) with its 0.5 x 45° chamfer and R0.4 root, the flange's other face to the 9.00 thickness, and the outside's second 0.5 x 45° chamfer

workholding.note: Lying flat on 1.25 in parallels under the flange, the first spigot hanging between them; the plain jaws grip the flange's 8 mm outside, whose band stands 32-40 mm above the vise floor, under the jaws' 44 mm top. The holes, at most 21 mm off the centre across the jaws, come out between the parallels, which stand 28.3 mm off it. A round part has nothing to clock it by, so the pattern's single hole is put along the jaws, +Y in the vise [proposed]

wcs.x: the centre of the top spigot (probe)
wcs.y: the centre of the top spigot (probe)
wcs.by: probe in X and Y, a boss cycle round the Ø31.5 spigot, and Z; tool setter for the tools' lengths

speeds.source: moonshot/sim/cam.py tool(): the plan's material rule, as G1's

operations.note: 6.5 mm is inside Ø6.6's ±0.2, and nearer its middle than the H drill (6.76 mm)

speeds.source: moonshot/sim/cam.py tool(): the plan's material rule, as G1's

finish.what: Deburr every edge, breaking each sharp corner 0.2 x 45° (note 1) with a hooked blade drawn along it, the five holes' edges on both faces too

finish.title: Check the spigots, the flange and the holes
finish.what: Check both Ø31.500 g6 spigots with the 1-2 in micrometer, the Ø63.0, the 9.00 flange, the 15.4 length and the holes' 25.00 and 17.68 positions with the calipers, and the five Ø6.6 holes with gauge pins

proposed.why: The Ø63.0 is ±0.3 (ISO 2768-m), so 0.25 mm a side cleans it up; 1 in gives Op 10 17.4 mm out of the jaws and 8 mm in them

proposed.what: Both lathe setups in one set of the Kitagawa's soft jaws, bored to Ø63.5
proposed.why: Op 10 grips the bar's Ø63.5 where Op 20 cuts it away; Op 20 grips the finished Ø63.0 in the same bore, closed 0.25 mm further, inside the drawing's general runout. Boring them isn't a step, as G1's soft jaws
The surface speed is the shop's rule for carbide in aluminium; no source gives the CCGT's and DCGT's feeds for this part

proposed.what: Op 30 on 1.25 in parallels in the plain jaws, the single hole along the jaws
proposed.why: A round part has no flat to clock it; the drawing doesn't place the pattern against anything but the axis
